gaps.sentence: Don't leave ___ any details in your report.
The hotel was full, so we couldn't check ___.
gaps.explanation: check in = register; check out = leave and pay.

gaps.sentence: It's time you faced up ___ your responsibilities.
gaps.explanation: face up TO something = accept and deal with something difficult.

gaps.sentence: She put her ideas ___ clearly and confidently.
gaps.explanation: put across = communicate an idea successfully.

gaps.sentence: I'm really looking forward to ___ you again soon.
gaps.explanation: look forward TO + -ing: 'to' is a preposition here.

gaps.sentence: She came ___ with a brilliant solution to the problem.
gaps.explanation: come up with = produce an idea/plan/solution.

gaps.sentence: The new manager wants to back ___ the sales team's proposal.
gaps.explanation: back up = support (a person, plan); also make a copy of data.

gaps.sentence: I've mixed ___ the twins' names again.
gaps.explanation: mix up = confuse one thing/person with another.
